name: Turkish Poker
description: Türk pokeri (Turkish Poker) is a five-card draw variant played with a short deck of 24 to 36 cards depending on player count. Each player receives five cards; up to four may be exchanged in the draw. Opening requires a pair of Kings; hand rankings differ from international poker (flush beats full house, three of a kind beats straight).

history.origins: Turkish poker (Türk pokeri) is a draw poker variant using a shortened French deck; information is attributed to Burçin Kerem Seyis. It follows the same deal–bet–draw–bet–showdown structure as five-card draw but with a minimum opening requirement of a pair of Kings and distinct hand rankings.
timeline: Contemporary: Turkish draw poker variant using a shortened French deck; information attributed to Burçin Kerem Seyis.
history.cultural: Played in Turkey with Turkish hand names (Floş, Kare, Ful, Üçlü, Kent, Doper, Per, Yüksek Kart).
history.evolution: Uses stripped deck (24–36 cards) and regional hand order: flush above full house, three of a kind above straight; suits break ties.

setup.deck: Short deck: 24 cards (2 players) through 36 cards (5 players), made by removing low cards from a standard 52-card pack.
setup.dealing: First dealer chosen at random; deal rotates left. Before each deal all players ante an equal amount. Cards are shuffled, cut, and dealt clockwise one at a time until each player has five cards.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the highest-ranked five-card hand at showdown or by being the last player left after all others fold.
rules.gameplay: 1. Ante: All players post an equal ante. 2. Deal: Five cards each, one at a time, clockwise. 3. First betting round: Minimum to open is a pair of Kings; players with less must pass; opener may pass. Once someone opens, others may call, raise, or fold. 4. Draw: Starting left of dealer, each player may exchange 0–4 cards (discard face down, receive replacements from stock). 5. Second betting round: Opener (or next active player) may check or bet; others fold, call, or raise. 6. Showdown: Remaining players reveal hands; highest hand wins. If nobody opens, hands are thrown in, pot stays, players ante again and the next dealer deals.
keyRules: Opening requirement: pair of Kings (oyunu açmak); less must pass (pas).
Draw: 0–4 cards exchanged; if requesting four, only three given initially then the fourth after all others served; discards shuffled and reused if stock runs out.
Hand order differs from international: flush beats full house; three of a kind beats straight; Ace can be low in minor straight; suits break ties (Hearts > Spades > Diamonds > Clubs).
Opener who folds or wins without showdown may be required to show cards to prove legal open (pair of Kings or better).

strategy.basic: Only open with a pair of Kings or better; fold weak hands before the draw; pay attention to how many cards opponents draw.
strategy.intermediate: Use position: opening from late position allows you to see more passes; drawing one card can represent a strong hand (straight or flush draw) and support bluffing.
strategy.advanced: Track suit ranking for tiebreaks; in marginal spots consider whether your hand benefits from the Turkish order (e.g. flush over full house); defend openers selectively when you suspect a bluff.
tips: If you request four cards, you receive three first and the fourth after everyone else is served.
Suit order for ties: Hearts (kupa) > Spades (maça) > Diamonds (karo) > Clubs (sinek).

scoring.description: Highest-ranked five-card hand at showdown wins the pot; last player remaining after all others fold wins without showdown.
scoring.winCondition: Highest hand at showdown wins the pot; or win by being the only player left in the hand.
